This release improves Jellyfin-native skip controls, managed-library refresh behavior, authentication visibility, and Docker playback safety. It also expands automated coverage and adds formatting/analyzer checks to both stable and nightly release pipelines.

### Licensing and Branding
- The repository is now licensed for non-commercial use under the **PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0**.
- Added explicit commercial licensing, trademark, and required-notice documents.
- Commercial use requires separate permission from the project owner; the AniLiberty STRM name and branding are not granted for unrestricted reuse.

### Docker Direct Play Guard
- Fixed automatic playback proxy URL selection inside Docker and other containers.
- The plugin no longer writes container-only bridge addresses such as `172.17.x.x` into generated `.strm` files.
- Proxy base URL priority is now: explicit **Jellyfin Playback Proxy Base URL**, `JELLYFIN_PublishedServerUrl`, then native-host auto-detection outside containers.
- When no client-reachable HTTP(S) base URL exists in a container, generation safely falls back to direct AniLiberty HLS URLs and records a clear task warning.
- Invalid manual or published proxy URLs are ignored instead of producing broken playback links.

### Native Skip Intro / Outro
- Replaced generated EDL and chapter XML skip files with a Jellyfin `IMediaSegmentProvider` implementation.
- Opening and ending timings are stored in `.aniliberty-strm-plugin/media-segments.json` and exposed as native Jellyfin media segments.
- Added background warm-up and path-to-episode reconciliation so existing library items receive updated skip timings without rewriting user-authored metadata.

### Managed Mirror and Metadata Refresh
- Expanded managed manifest tracking for STRM, NFO, artwork, popularity metadata, and media-segment state.
- Generated metadata is refreshed when the upstream AniLiberty signal changes while unmarked user-authored files remain protected.
- Cleanup remains bounded to plugin-managed files, with `Keep`, `DryRun`, and opt-in `Delete` behavior.
- Improved specials, franchise-season, fractional-ordinal, hydration, and image-handling paths.

### Popularity and Authentication Visibility
- Added an optional AniLiberty popularity badge to Jellyfin Web item pages.
- Added a public, read-only metadata endpoint backed only by plugin-generated popularity sidecars.
- Added Jellyfin activity notifications when a stored AniLiberty token starts returning HTTP 401/403, with cooldown protection against notification spam.
- Improved login/password, OTP, favorites, and watch-timecode API handling and validation.

### Playback and Sync Reliability
- Kept HLS playlist and segment delivery streaming through Jellyfin without buffering complete media objects in memory.
- Improved STRM URL normalization, playlist route handling, redirect validation, and playback diagnostics.
- Improved per-session watch-progress coordination, cancellation, path resolution, and forward-only progress updates.

### Quality Gates and Verification
- Added `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` to stable and nightly workflows, covering formatting and built-in Roslyn analyzer diagnostics without an extra linter dependency.
- Expanded automated coverage across controllers, API clients, scheduled tasks, managed cleanup, native media segments, popularity injection, authentication notifications, and Docker proxy URL selection.
- Full release-gated result: **207/207 non-integration tests passed**, clean Debug and Release builds, and zero compiler warnings. Three opt-in live AniLiberty API checks remain outside the release gate.
- Reproduced the Docker failure on Jellyfin 10.11.11: an internal bridge URL caused `DirectPlayError` and ffmpeg fallback; a client-reachable proxy URL played the same H.264/AAC stream through Direct Play with no transcoding.

### Upgrade Notes
- Restart Jellyfin after installing the update.
- Run **Generate AniLiberty STRM library** again so existing `.strm` files and managed state receive the new routing and metadata behavior.
- Docker users who want Jellyfin-proxied playback should set **Jellyfin Playback Proxy Base URL** or `JELLYFIN_PublishedServerUrl` to an address reachable by playback devices and the Jellyfin container.

### Not Included
- No Jellyfin 10.10 compatibility build.
- No full-segment server-side cache or mid-segment resume; brief client-side HLS buffering remains the current protection against connection jitter.
- No change to AniLiberty API endpoint hosts or the legacy GitHub Pages repository URL.
- No season-gap fix: the reported missing-season case was not established as a plugin defect in this work.

AniLiberty STRM Support Trace & Docker Preflight

Release 2.0.0.9
AniLiberty STRM Hardening System Release

This update hardens AniLiberty STRM Plugin as a full Jellyfin reconstruction system: stable Jellyfin ABI targeting, explicit AniLiberty identity, safer generated-library governance, streaming playback proxying, and a stronger operational surface for administrators.

### Jellyfin Compatibility & Quality Gates
- Pinned all `Jellyfin.*` NuGet references to `10.11.0` to stop builds from silently drifting to newer Jellyfin packages.
- Added committed `packages.lock.json` files and locked restore in CI.
- Added CI checks that verify every resolved `Jellyfin.*` package remains on `10.11.0` while `targetAbi` stays `10.11.0.0`.
- Release automation now keeps `build.yaml`, package version, assembly version, file version, and informational version in sync.

### AniLiberty Identity & API Courtesy
- Rebranded the public plugin identity to **AniLiberty STRM Plugin** while keeping the legacy `AniLibriaStrmPlugin` repository URL for install compatibility and branch history.
- Added a shared `PluginIdentity` with display name, product token, repository URL, version discovery, and canonical User-Agent.
- All AniLiberty API, media proxy, static media, and HLS clients now identify as:
  `AniLibertyStrmPlugin/<version> (Jellyfin; +https://github.com/queukat/AniLibriaStrmPlugin)`.

### Mirror Governance Layer
- Added `.aniliberty-strm-plugin/manifest.json` inside each output root to track files managed by the plugin.
- The manifest records generated STRM, ANIID, EDL, chapter XML, NFO, artwork/thumbs, release/episode IDs, hashes, sources, and timestamps.
- First manifest run initializes the baseline and never prunes existing files.
- Generated NFO/artwork refreshes only when the file is known as plugin-managed through the manifest or generated marker.
- Existing unmarked `.nfo` files and artwork are preserved as user-owned content.

### Safe Cleanup Modes
- Added `StaleCleanupMode`: `Off`, `DryRun`, and `Delete`.
- Default is `DryRun`, which reports stale managed files without deleting anything.
- `Delete` removes only manifest-managed stale files and then removes empty directories created by that cleanup path.
- Untracked user files are left alone.

### Playback Proxy Rail
- Non-playlist HLS segments and keys now stream directly to `Response.Body`.
- The proxy no longer reads segment/key payloads into memory with `ReadAsByteArrayAsync`.
- Upstream host allow-listing and redirect validation remain in place.
- Playlist rewriting continues to route segments and keys through the Jellyfin proxy endpoint.

### Identity & Access Command Center
- OTP codes are no longer persisted in plugin configuration after the OTP flow.
- Login/password and OTP sign-in clear stored OTP state.
- The token box is masked by default, with explicit reveal/copy actions.
- Auth logs no longer include the login e-mail address.

### Operational Reliability
- Scheduled tasks now rethrow failures after logging so Jellyfin can mark task execution accurately.
- Cancellation flows are preserved instead of being swallowed as generic failures.
- AniLiberty progress pull no longer overwrites newer local Jellyfin playback positions with older remote timecodes.
- Clearing UI logs now persists the cleared state.

### Presentation & Documentation
- README now presents the plugin as a coherent product system: Signal Acquisition Layer, Context-Aware Reconstruction Core, Playback Proxy Rail, Mirror Governance Layer, Operational Command Center, and Distribution Quality Gates.
- Added three README visual assets showing the reconstruction core, system capability layers, and operational command center.

### Test Coverage
- Added tests for Jellyfin package pins and lock-file resolution.
- Added User-Agent and named/static HTTP client coverage.
- Added managed mirror tests for baseline creation, generated metadata refresh, unmarked NFO preservation, dry-run cleanup, delete cleanup, and empty-directory cleanup.
- Added proxy tests for streaming segments, playlist rewriting, unsupported upstream rejection, redirect validation, and upstream failure status.
- Added auth/config tests for OTP payload boundaries, safe defaults, and AniLiberty identity.

### Not Included
- No Jellyfin 10.10 compatibility build in this release.
- No migration of AniLiberty API endpoint hosts.
- No destructive cleanup unless `StaleCleanupMode` is explicitly changed to `Delete`.

# AniLiberty API v1 Alignment, Better Metadata & Quieter Logs

This update improves AniLiberty authentication reliability, aligns the plugin with AniLiberty API v1 responses, and enhances generated metadata while keeping UI logs under control.

## Authentication & OTP
- Improved login and OTP endpoints with proper HTTP status codes and safer request validation.
- Updated OTP parsing to support the API v1 format (`otp.code`) and kept backward compatibility for older responses.
- OTP flow in the settings UI is simplified to **Start → Sign In** (the “Accept OTP” UI action was removed).

## Networking reliability
- Switched API calls to a reusable, DI-managed `HttpClient` (`IHttpClientFactory`) with consistent headers (User-Agent / Accept / Accept-Language).
- Added retry handling for rate limits (**HTTP 429**) and transient errors.
- Optimized HTTP reads using `ResponseHeadersRead` to reduce overhead and improve responsiveness.

## STRM generation & metadata quality
- Better year handling for AniLiberty v1 (`release.year` instead of `season.year`), including TV show year selection across grouped seasons.
- More accurate content classification:
  - Detects **MOVIE** by API `type.value` when available.
  - Routes **SPECIAL / OVA / OAD** into **Season 00** more reliably.
- Improved image handling:
  - Supports v1 image schema (`preview/thumbnail/optimized`) and prefers non-optimized URLs when possible.
  - Normalizes `.webp` URLs to `.jpg` and safely determines thumbnail file extensions even when URLs contain query parameters.
- Episode NFO improvements:
  - Writes episode titles (RU/EN when available), runtime, year, and sets `lockdata=false`.

## Logging & settings
- Added **“Enable debug logs (very noisy)”** setting:
  - When OFF: DEBUG/TRACE aren’t stored in UI logs and per-title progress logging is throttled to avoid bloating the UI log.
- UI log filtering now respects minimum log level and the debug toggle.

## Developer / maintenance
- Manual generation test is now **skipped by default** and uses environment variables (`ANI_TOKEN`, `ANI_OUTPUT_DIR`) so tokens aren’t stored in the repo.
- Internal null-safety improvements around plugin initialization.

## Not included
- No changes to library scanning behavior or broader UI redesign beyond the OTP/auth/logging settings shown above.

description:
Manage your server's afterlife. Identify lifeless media, condemn dead weight to The Chapel, and track your active Visitors.

versions.changelog: Adds Hidden viewers: tick users in Settings to leave them out of The Guestbook and The Sanctuary, so one person watching a single show on repeat no longer drowns out everyone else's stats. Their plays still count in The Morgue and The Chapel, so a show only they watch is never offered up for deletion as unwatched.

Makes the optional "Leaving Soon" home screen row look native. It previously sat flush against the page edge while every other row was indented, with undersized posters and a stray link below the section. It now uses the web client's own section and card markup, so spacing, sizing, hover and focus match the rest of the home screen.

Fixes the public "Leaving Soon: The Chapel" collection being empty. Condemning an item that already carried the tag never added it to the collection, so anything condemned by an earlier version was invisible to viewers. Condemning is idempotent now, and a Sync collection button on the Chapel tab adds everything already tagged. Also fixes the optional home screen row never appearing after a slow load or a login.

Adds an optional "Leaving Soon" row to the home screen listing what is in The Chapel — off by default, and hidden while The Chapel is empty. The Chapel collection also stops telling viewers that a deletion deadline exists: nothing expires, and Last Rites remains a deliberate act by the server owner.

Fixes the Guestbook failing on Jellyfin 10.11.9 and newer, where an API change made it error out. Also: stored XSS and webhook authentication fixes; Plays, Time Played and Reach now reconcile; a rebuilt dashboard with loading, empty and error states; cached aggregates instead of a library walk per row; and a test suite. Minimum server is 10.11.6.
The Chapel Update: Automated collection branding, thematic iconography, and .NET 9 performance optimizations.
Initial Release: Opening the gates to Graveyard Analytics v1.0.

- Fixed plugin failing to load on Jellyfin 10.11.0-10.11.10 ("incompatible version of one of the shared libraries", issue #19): now built against Jellyfin 10.11.0 instead of the latest 10.11.x
- Jellyfin 12 build now targets the final 12.0.0 packages instead of 12.0.0-rc2
- Fixed missing plugin logo (and 404 on disable/uninstall) on Jellyfin 12: the Jellyfin 12 DLL reported version 1.1.0.0 instead of its package version; each build now carries its own version (10.11 = 1.1.0.x, Jellyfin 12 = 1.1.1.x)
- Fixed a crashed client's ghost session getting the user's new, legitimate stream stopped (up to ~10 min lockout): the PlaybackStart limiter now uses the same fresh-check-in, per-device count as the HTTP gate
- Transcode kill no longer falls back to killing every job of the device when the client sent no PlaySessionId
- Custom web message now works on servers with a BaseUrl (the injected script used an absolute /StreamLimit path)
Jellyfin 12 build of v1.1.0.1 (same changes — see the 1.1.0.1 entry). Servers pick the right build automatically: 10.11 installs 1.1.0.1, Jellyfin 12 installs 1.1.1.1.

- NEW (BETA): HTTP-level hard block — over-limit streams are rejected before any byte is served; works on every client (Swiftfin, Infuse, external players)
- NEW (BETA): single clean custom message on web clients (replaces the built-in dialog)
- NEW: default max streams for users without an explicit limit
- NEW: config migration from pre-1.1 installs (normalizes legacy entries)
- Fixed silent failure where one invalid config entry disabled every limit (#5/#8/#18)
- Fixed device logout (a session id was passed where an access token was expected)
- Kill transcode jobs of blocked streams; optional device logout
- Admin-only stream limit API; removed Newtonsoft.Json
- Fixed duplicated users in the config page dropdown (#16) and empty popup (#6)
Jellyfin 12 build of v1.1.0.0 (same features — see the 1.1.0.0 entry). Servers pick the right build automatically: 10.11 installs 1.1.0.0, Jellyfin 12 installs 1.1.1.0.
- Updated to 10.11 compatible version

versions.changelog: # 🚀 A New Foundation for File Transformation File Transformation **3.0.0.0** is a major overhaul of how the plugin integrates with Jellyfin. The transformation system has been rebuilt around standard ASP.NET Core middleware, removing much of the version-specific runtime patching that File Transformation previously relied on. Alongside **Jellyfin 12 support**, this release drops support for **Jellyfin 10.10.7** and lays a much more maintainable foundation for future Jellyfin releases. > ## 🙌 Huge thanks to @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv > > A massive part of this release is thanks to **@4eh5xitv6787h645ebv**, who took on the major overhaul of File Transformation's core architecture in PR #58. > > The move away from the old Harmony/MonoMod-based interception system to standard ASP.NET Core middleware is a significant piece of work. It not only makes File Transformation substantially easier to maintain, but also resolves an entire class of compatibility problems that caused the plugin to malfunction or be disabled on certain Jellyfin versions and platforms (#20, #35, #62, #64, #70, #71). > > This is far more than a small patch or isolated feature - it fundamentally improves the foundation the plugin is built on. A huge thank you for the time and effort that went into it. ## ✨ New Features * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and the newer Jellyfin server architecture (#34). * Replaced the previous Harmony/MonoMod-based web interception system with standard ASP.NET Core `IStartupFilter` middleware (PR #58, @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv). * Added support for unregistering transformations through `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing dependent plugins to cleanly remove transformations when required. * Added support for synthesising virtual files for registered transformation paths, restoring support for plugins such as Plugin Pages where the underlying file doesn't physically exist. * Added ETag generation and `304 Not Modified` support for transformed content. * Added Brotli and gzip recompression of transformed responses for remote clients. * Added automatic MIME type detection for virtual transformed files. ## 🛠️ Improvements * Removed platform-specific DLL extraction and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * Removed dependencies on Harmony, MonoMod and Prometheus from the core transformation pipeline. * Improved compatibility across Jellyfin versions and platforms by moving the transformation system onto standard ASP.NET Core APIs (#20, #35, #62, #64). * Added per-transformation error isolation so a failure in one plugin's transformation won't prevent other transformations from running. * Made transformation registration, removal and execution thread-safe. * Added regex caching and timeout protection for transformation matching. * Improved handling of `Accept-Encoding`, including proper quality-value (`q`) parsing. * Improved LAN detection for IPv6-mapped IPv4 addresses. * Improved proxy caching behaviour by correctly setting `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. * Reworked HTTP handling to use a shared `HttpClient` with appropriate timeouts. * Hardened named-pipe transformations with timeouts, size limits, EOF handling and improved resource cleanup. ## 🪲 Bug Fixes * Fixed a class of failures where Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching could cause File Transformation to malfunction or be automatically disabled on startup (#20, #35, #62, #64, #71). * Fixed #70 where transformations could attempt to use a disposed `IServiceProvider` after Jellyfin restarted, resulting in `500` responses across the web UI. * Fixed transformed content potentially retaining stale trailing bytes when a transformation produced a shorter result than the original response. * Fixed failures in one transformation potentially breaking the entire transformation pipeline. * Fixed potential `HttpClient` resource leaks. * Fixed named-pipe transformations being able to hang indefinitely or loop on zero-byte reads. * Fixed incorrect handling of disabled compression encodings such as `gzip;q=0`. * Fixed failed virtual-file transformations returning an empty successful response instead of reverting to the original `404`. * Improved middleware failure handling so the original response is served if transformation or recompression fails. ## 💻 Developer Compatibility The existing `PluginInterface.RegisterTransformation` API and registration payload remain compatible with previous releases, so plugins using a standard transformation callback **should not need to change how they register transformations**. There are, however, some changes to transformation execution that plugin developers should be aware of: * Added `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing plugins to explicitly unregister a previously registered transformation. * Assembly callbacks still receive the same payload and are expected to return the transformed content as a `string`. * Invalid or failed assembly callbacks now **fail safely rather than falling through to another configured callback mechanism**. Plugins should ensure their callback assembly, class and method names are valid. * HTTP transformation callbacks must now return a **successful HTTP status code**. Non-success responses are treated as a failed transformation rather than using the response body as transformed content. * HTTP callbacks now have a **15 second timeout**. * Named-pipe callbacks now have connection/error handling and a **50 MB maximum response size**. * Failed transformations now leave the original response untouched rather than potentially replacing it with invalid or partial output. These changes are intended to make transformations significantly safer and more predictable, but plugins relying on the previous fallback or error behaviour should review their integrations when updating. ## ⚠️ Compatibility * **Jellyfin 10.10.7 is no longer supported.** * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and its newer server architecture (#34). * Users remaining on Jellyfin 10.10.7 will need to stay on an earlier File Transformation release until they upgrade Jellyfin. * Removed legacy Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * File Transformation now relies on standard ASP.NET Core middleware rather than patching Jellyfin internals, providing a much more stable base for future Jellyfin versions. ## Contributors * 4eh5xitv6787h645ebv ## ❤️ Support If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27). Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.

name: Jellyfin Helper [✓✓✓]
description:
Cleans up orphaned .trickplay folders, empty media folders, and orphaned subtitles. Repairs broken .strm files and symlinks. Scheduled Seerr cleanup of unavailable Overseerr/Jellyseerr media requests. Provides media library statistics with video/audio codec analysis, resolution/container/bitrate/language breakdown, Library Explorer search, dynamic range detection (HDR10, HDR10+, Dolby Vision, HLG, SDR), health checks (embedded subtitle detection), caching, ML-powered smart recommendations per user with ensemble scoring (heuristic, learned, neural), Seerr Discovery for personalized external content suggestions with one-click request submission, user activity insights with play count and completion tracking, library insights (largest directories & recent changes), historical trends, trash/recycle bin with detailed contents UI, multi-instance Arr stack integration (up to 3 Radarr + 3 Sonarr) with connection testing and collapsible UI, plugin-specific log viewer with download and filtering, unsaved settings protection, and a multi-language 8-tab dashboard (en, de, fr, es, pt, zh, tr, sv).  
  
Universal Repo 
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JellyPlugins/jellyfin-helper/main/manifest.json  
Github: https://github.com/JellyPlugins/jellyfin-helper
overview: Automated cleanup (trickplay, empty folders, subtitles, link repair for .strm & symlinks), Seerr request cleanup, Seerr Discovery (personalized external content recommendations with one-click requests), media statistics with codec/health/dynamic-range analysis and Library Explorer search, ML-powered smart recommendations per user, user activity insights, library insights, trends, trash bin, plugin log viewer, multi-instance Arr integration, unsaved settings alert, and multi-language 8-tab dashboard.

versions.changelog:
v3.0.1.2 - Discovery background work respects its master switch, Trakt travels with backup

- Seerr discovery generation and the Trakt refresh no longer run while Discovery user access is off; stored choices resume automatically on re-enabling
- Backup export/import round-trips the "Enable Trakt discovery" flag, so the choice survives a move to a fresh installation
- The Trakt checkbox only appears with Discovery on and the official Trakt plugin detected, and auto-saves like the Discovery toggle
- DryRun warms discovery caches without persisting, and leaves the shared trending pool untouched
- Greyed-out settings are now truly inert (keyboard and screen readers), and unsaved-changes tracking no longer reports phantom edits
- Tested by 6800 unit tests and 369 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.2 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.1.1 - "Trakt for you" no longer stays empty; discovery is quieter and self-healing

- Fixed the main report: "Trakt for you" could stay empty while trending and the local picks were full. Virtual stub library entries (real-looking files with a TMDb id but no media, created by some request helpers) were counted as owned and silently excluded every personal pick. They are now recognised as virtual and ignored, so your Trakt recommendations come through
- An empty "Trakt for you" is no longer sticky: a null or empty result is cached only briefly, so once the server has your picks they appear on the next open instead of being held behind a stale empty view
- A rate-limited or unreachable Trakt is retried with a backoff (honouring the server's Retry-After) instead of being re-hit on every tab load, and the same account open on two devices now shares one fetch instead of firing two
- An unlinked user no longer sees a "Trakt for you" tab that only shows a not-linked message; the tab appears once you are linked, and "Trakt trending" (which needs no login) is always available
- The plugin log now explains an empty personal result in one line (what was fetched, what survived, and why), so a token, fetch, or ownership issue is far easier to pin down
- Tested by 6779 unit tests and 369 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.2 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6
- Special thanks to @TheColin21 (https://github.com/TheColin21) for finding and reporting the empty "Trakt for you" issue and for debugging it together ❤️

v3.0.1.0 - Trakt discovery + encrypted secrets, Discovery tab no longer goes blank on Jellyfin 12

- New Trakt discovery source: when the official Jellyfin Trakt plugin is installed, the Discovery tab gains two sub-tabs beside the local picks, "Trakt for you" (your personal Trakt recommendations) and "Trakt trending" (global, no login), using the same card layout, request/dismiss mechanics, and per-user ML scoring. The Helper has no Trakt app of its own: it sources everything read-only through the official plugin's connection, so there is nothing to configure per user and no second app to register. A single "Enable Trakt discovery" checkbox (shown only when the official plugin is detected) turns it on
- All stored credentials (Seerr and Arr API keys) are now encrypted at rest with Data Protection and never logged in plain text; backups stay portable and re-encrypt on restore
- The Seerr Discovery custom tab reliably shows its content again on Jellyfin 12: navigating away and back no longer leaves it blank
- Returning to the tab is instant and never flashes a spinner: the last results render immediately from memory, and newer suggestions are swapped in silently in the background when a scheduled run has produced them
- The sidebar "Seerr Discovery" link opens the tab correctly on the modern Jellyfin 12 layout (both the top header and the narrow-screen menu), as well as on the classic layout
- The Codecs tab cards can now be rearranged by dragging a card's header handle (long-press on touch, with edge auto-scroll) or by keyboard (Enter to grab, arrow keys to move, Enter to drop, Escape to cancel); the order saves instantly, survives refresh/restart/update, and travels with backup export/import
- Radarr/Sonarr instances behind a reverse proxy with a private CA, self-signed, or IP certificate can now connect via a per-instance "Skip certificate validation" checkbox in Settings
- Recommendations now follow completed franchises: a series you finished years ago is surfaced again when a new entry arrives, instead of being outranked by whatever you watched most recently
- Recommendation explanations are now concrete: the "Why" line names what actually drove the pick (completing a collection, a franchise, a matched writer/country/era, or genuine crowd popularity) instead of a vague "Recommended for you". Discovery suggestions keep their person/genre/trending/popularity reasons, now with an honest fallback instead of claiming "Popular and highly rated" for a title that is neither
- Hardening: API keys, the log filter, and backup credentials now reject hidden control characters that could cause errors or log tampering; odd-charset responses are read safely; and restoring a backup that disables TLS validation now warns you first
- Recommendation playlists are always private: playlist sync now sets visibility explicitly instead of relying on the server default, so each user's recommendations stay visible to that user only
- Tested by 6720 unit tests (expanded security, hardening, and performance coverage) and 368 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.2 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6
- Special thanks to @TheColin21 (https://github.com/TheColin21) for testing and donation ❤️
- Special thanks to Daniel for his donation ❤️
- Special thanks to @baervers23 (https://github.com/baervers23) for great input and ideas ❤️

v3.0.0.4 - Per-library file counts, boxset link fix

- The Per-Library Breakdown now shows a file count below every size value (trickplay folders included), so sparse and dense libraries are distinguishable at a glance
- Boxset library rows no longer link into the Library Explorer, whose scope excludes boxsets; they render as plain text instead of opening an empty state
- Every task dropdown in Settings now explains what the task does, via an info button next to each task name, in all dashboard languages
- The Overview Trickplay card now also shows the space used by trickplay images Jellyfin stores internally, on its own line below the alongside-media total, marked with an (internal) badge, or as the headline when no alongside data exists
- Compact log view on phones: log entries stack as cards below 700 px instead of squeezing into a four-column table, so no horizontal scrolling is needed, and rows keep breathing room at the screen edges
- Roomier Library Explorer filter popovers on phones using nearly the full viewport width, like the bitrate editor
- Tested by 6219 unit tests and 352 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.1 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.3 - Library Explorer, new Codecs breakdowns, disabled users ignored

- The Codecs tab now has a Library Explorer: combine resolution, codecs, bitrate, languages, watched users and formats into one search, scoped to the libraries you pick in its multi-select, so you can find e.g. all 4K films with low bitrate
- Options with zero matches under the other filters are hidden automatically, dimensions without matches stay greyed out, and multi-value dropdowns accept several audio languages, subtitle languages or users at once
- Every active filter is shown in the result header and a Reset button clears the whole search; results arrive as the familiar grouped file tree with Movies, TV Shows and other sections
- Jump straight into the search from the Overview: each library name and all four media cards open the Explorer pre-filtered to that scope
- Every categorical filter can be negated with Includes/Excludes, so you can search e.g. audio languages that are not German; excluded picks show as ≠ pills and counts preview what stays
- Four new breakdowns in the Codecs tab, each with drill-down to the exact files: Video Bitrate (7 tiers from < 2 to > 60 Mbps), Audio Languages, Subtitle Languages and Watched (by username plus Never watched)
- Each bitrate tier uses what Jellyfin measured for the video stream; when a file has no per-stream value the average is estimated from its size and runtime, so almost every file lands in a real tier instead of Unknown
- Disabled Jellyfin users no longer skew results: their old plays are excluded from Smart Recommendations, watch history and the new Watched breakdown
- Long breakdowns start collapsed behind a Show-all toggle with Unknown always last, and unreadable language tags fold into Unknown instead of junk entries
- Added responsive, independently scrollable library result cards.
- Improved compact layouts for mobile controls.
- Added consistent themed scrollbar styling across plugin panels and lists.
- The Overview Per-Library Breakdown has a new Other column per library covering NFO files, text files and other unrecognized sidecar files, plus a Books column whenever a book library exists, so every row adds up exactly to its Total
- Tested by 6169 unit tests and 341 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.1 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.2 - Log tab, save bar, resolution and touch fixes

- Clearing the plugin log no longer briefly shows a false "Failed to clear logs." error: the Clear button now confirms success immediately and refreshes the view right away
- Genuine clear failures (e.g. expired session or server error) now write a structured diagnostic to the browser console with the HTTP status and error kind, alongside the visible red button feedback, so a real problem is never silent
- Save bar no longer crowds on phones: the unsaved-changes label and Save button now stack on narrow screens, so long translations like the German "Nicht gespeichert" are no longer cut off
- Widescreen films are counted at their real resolution: cinemascope masters like 1920x800 or 1920x1040 are now correctly shown as 1080p instead of 720p in the Codecs tab, decided by whichever axis reaches a resolution class
- The resolution drill-down now lists each file's exact pixel dimensions (e.g. 1920x800) next to its name, readable on desktop and phones
- Chart tooltips work reliably on touch: the first tap on the Trends chart or a Codecs ring now shows and keeps the tooltip instead of flashing it away, and a second tap on the same Codecs segment closes it
- The save confirmation only appears after a real save: reverting a setting back to its original value no longer briefly shows "All changes saved"
- Tested by 5535 unit tests and 320 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.0 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.1 - Per-instance library allocation for Arr

- Assign specific Jellyfin libraries to each Radarr/Sonarr instance, so the Arr tab compares an instance only against the libraries it manages
- With two or more instances of a type, each gets a picker in Settings listing only the matching kind of library (movies for Radarr, TV for Sonarr)
- Leave a picker empty to keep it automatic: instances are matched to libraries from their root folders
- Assignments are kept across backup and restore
- Fixes a 4K instance flagging every 1080p film as "not in Radarr"
- Tested by 5499 unit tests and 318 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.0 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.0 - Major release for Jellyfin 12.0+

- Books in your library overview: eBook libraries now show their size and file count on the Overview tab and count towards your storage totals, and they're always protected from every cleanup task
- Smarter recommendations: a much bigger model, fairer suggestions for brand-new users, and more variety in your top picks (no more ten near-identical films in a row)
- Recommendations now also learn from franchises/collections, country of origin, collection & folder themes, whether a series is finished or ongoing, writers/creators, top-billed cast, and how rare a genre or studio is in your library (each signal is optional per item, so missing metadata never skews a pick)
- Fresh picks appear between nightly runs, and faster generation on big libraries
- Redesigned Settings, Health and Arr tabs with a live 'reachable' indicator, plus a sticky save bar and unsaved-changes warning
- Better on phones
- Stronger security: API keys are never shown to the browser, backups can leave keys out, and cleanup can never delete or touch anything outside your media libraries
- Safer trash and cleanup: turning retention off really turns it off, trashing a shortcut never removes the file it points to, and Windows shortcut handling is fixed
- More accurate library stats and safer Seerr request cleanup
- More reliable saves and backups (no more rare 'lost save' when antivirus is scanning)
- New end-to-end test suite runs the plugin inside a real Jellyfin 12 server on every change and proves cleanup stays inside your libraries
- Note: your recommendation model retrains from scratch after upgrading, so suggestions settle back in over the next scheduled runs
- Requires Jellyfin 12.0 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v2.1.0.6: Diagnostics for reverse-proxy / WAF-blocked config saves. Added GET /JellyfinHelper/Ping liveness endpoint. Configuration model-binding and validation errors are now logged to the plugin log (source "API", level WARN) instead of silently returning 400. Frontend save handler now classifies errors (network / proxy / server / unauthorized) and surfaces the HTTP status and body snippet to the console, with an automatic Ping follow-up to distinguish "backend unreachable" from "backend reachable, payload rejected". 2325 tests.

v2.1.0.5: Fix StackOverflow on circular symlinks in directory scan. Fix IOException on long trash path names. Added Swedish (sv) language. Exclude Libraries multi-select dropdown. Trash folder browser. Trash path change dialog (move/delete content on path change). Enhanced trash path validation. Upgraded to Jellyfin 10.11.10. 2318 tests.
v2.1.0.4: Fix MissingMethodException for IUserManager.Users.

v2.1.0.3: Add TMDB and Seerr deep links on discovery card flip-back (opens system browser on mobile). Fix 400 Bad Request when submitting discovery requests on Seerr instances with 0-based server IDs. Fix duplicate quality profiles in selection popup for users with multiple root folders. Add graceful error handling for Jellyfin version incompatibility in watch history collection. 2206 tests
v2.1.0.2: Improved Discovery Sidebar Navigation - tab layout can show more than 5 recommendations in one row now. Automatically reloading next recommendation after one was dismissed or requested.
v2.1.0.1: Fix Discovery sidebar navigation - tab is now found dynamically by container index regardless of user-configured tab name, instead of relying on exact text match.

v2.1.0.0: Seerr Discovery - personalized external content recommendations via Overseerr/Jellyseerr with ensemble scoring, one-click request submission, parental rating enforcement, language-based discovery, and Arr library exclusion. 2190 tests.

v2.0.0.3: Instance-based Arr config (legacy removed), persistent language/log-level. Recommendations add audio language & creation date, subtitle language affinity, collection progression boost; meaningful-interaction watched predicates. Centralized popularity scoring, richer training features (31-feature vector), series aggregation, weight schema bump. Neural MLP upgraded to 4-hidden-layer architecture (31→48→24→12→6→1, ~3097 params). Training refactored into TrainingDataBuilder + TrainingFeatureComputer. A/B testing cohort infrastructure with deterministic user bucketing and adaptive sigmoid midpoint. 2124 tests.

v2.0.0.2: Replaced decorative emojis with Material Symbols font icons for consistent cross-platform rendering. Standardized dash punctuation. Fixed subtitle orphan detection to avoid false deletions. 2110 tests.
v2.0.0.1: UI improvement - Recommendations and Watch Activity sections in the Discover tab are now collapsible. Collapsible state is preserved on user switch. 2032 tests.

v2.0.0.0: New Discover tab using an ensemble ML model to provide tailored content recommendations. This update also introduces granular activity tracking and improved system cleanup for uninstallation of this plugin. 2032 tests.

v1.2.1.0: Statistics refactored to use Jellyfin MediaStream metadata (replaces filename parsing). Dynamic range detection (HDR10, HDR10+, Dolby Vision, HLG, SDR). Extended resolution classification (8K, 1440p, SD). Differentiated audio codecs (TrueHD Atmos, DTS-X, DTS-HD MA, EAC3 Atmos). Donut chart enhancements with dynamic range visualization. Library Insights in Trends tab (top-10 largest directories, recently added/changed items, per-library size breakdown with 15-min cache). Performance improvement via per-item video stream caching. Documentation updated.

v1.2.0.0: Seerr Cleanup Task (scheduled cleanup of unavailable Overseerr/Jellyseerr media requests), Unsaved Settings Alert (dirty-tracking with discard/save/cancel dialog), Collapsible Arr/Seerr sections with dynamic instance count, Auto-Save Dropdowns (task modes + language save instantly with checkmark/cross indicator), Link Repair enhanced with symlink support, Auto-Init Scan on first visit, Scroll Position Restore after language change and backup import, 4-part versioning, meta.json fixes.
v1.1.0: Performance optimizations for GrowthTimelineService and BackupService, refactored monolith services, improved cross-platform compatibility, Trends UI enhancements.

v1.0.9: Removed legacy statistics history (replaced by growth timeline), removed Export/CSV endpoints, new StatisticsCacheService, legacy history file cleanup, growth timeline interpolation & deduplication, reduced backup size limit, 957 tests.
v1.0.8: Project restructure, bug fix for Jellyfin versions below 10.11.8, backup/restore data, enhanced TrendChart, relocated download buttons, responsive Data Tree for touch devices.

v1.0.7: Added i18n support (EN, DE, FR, ES, PT, TR, ZH), scheduled task for cleaning empty media folders, trend chart visualization, configurable intervals, and automatic plugin data directory creation.
Exclude trash folders from media statistics, fix false positives for orphaned TV show metadata directories, fix trash disable dialog in UI.

Multi-instance Arr support (up to 3 Radarr + 3 Sonarr), Arr connection test endpoint, persisted latest scan results (survives restarts), post-cleanup statistics scan, embedded subtitle detection in health checks, video vs music audio codec split, codec file path tracking with clickable drill-down, trash contents detail API, trash folder management UI, trash disable dialog, other file tracking, 6-tab modular dashboard (Overview/Codecs/Health/Trends/Settings/Arr), modular CSS/JS build system, XSS protection, boxset/collection health check skipping, comprehensive README rewrite, 573 tests.

Added STRM file repair task, unified TaskMode system (Activate/DryRun/Deactivate per task), single master HelperCleanupTask replacing separate scheduled tasks, fixed ConfigVersion not preserved on settings save, fixed DI resolution for System.IO.Abstractions.IFileSystem, updated README, 315 tests.

Fixed plugin logo 404 (logo.png now included as physical file in release ZIP with meta.json imagePath), fixed SanitizeFileName null-char handling, removed duplicate Cleanup Statistics UI section, removed unused GetThumbImage method, 244 tests.

Fixed subtitle false positives (explicit ISO 639 allowlists instead of naive 2-3 letter heuristic), moved SubtitleFlags/KnownLanguageCodes to MediaExtensions, ArrIntegrationService now uses IHttpClientFactory, CleanupTrackingService thread-safety with lock, specific exception handling, removed _ = ex anti-pattern, 244 tests.
Fixed config page not loading (script/style tags moved inside page div), plugin now visible in Jellyfin sidebar menu with EnableInMainMenu, updated test count to 212.

versions.changelog:
## Developer
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.16.

## Features
- Frames are no longer taken from inside media segments, so intros, credits, recaps, previews, and commercials stay out of generated artwork
- New Avoid Media Segments setting under Frame Extraction, with a checkbox for each kind of segment to avoid, all on by default
- Segments come from a media segment provider turned on for the library, so items without any extract as before

## Developer
- Changing which segments are avoided discards the idle frame pools, so the next refresh extracts under the new choice

## Features
- New Cleanup Backdrops scheduled task under Library that reduces every item on the server to a single backdrop, keeping the first and deleting the rest along with their files
- The task has no default schedule, so it only runs when started by hand or on a trigger you add

## Features
- Primary and thumb images can name a second and third design, adding their versions of the same frames to the Edit Images picker
- New Edit Images Cache setting for how long rendered choices stay available, default 30 minutes
- Edit Images reuses the choices it already rendered when switching image type or page, instead of rendering every image again

## Fixes
- The Edit Images cache is bounded by size at 256 MB and releases expired images on its own, instead of holding them until the next render
- Every design in one Edit Images render draws from the same frames, even while other items are extracting
- Posters pass over a logo Jellyfin only knows by web address and use the next logo that can be read

## Developer
- Settings saved before 12.0.2.0 are no longer brought forward, so update through 12.0.2.1 first when coming from an older version
- Code, pages, and docs say logo rather than series logo, since films draw their own

## Fixes
- The Profiles page loads again instead of failing on a backdrop setting that no longer exists
- Posters with a logo draw the logo selected for a film, season, or series instead of falling back to text

## Features
- Artwork Generator is Episode Poster Generator rebuilt, with the same settings and a much wider job
- The repository moved with the name; re-add it as jellyfin-plugin-artworkgenerator to keep getting updates
- Draws posters, thumbs, backdrops, and text logos, where before there were only episode posters
- Covers series, seasons, films, music videos, home videos, and anything else with a video
- Configuration is rebuilt in three parts, designs, logos, and profiles
- Profiles decide which items get which images and which design draws each one
- Every design renders portrait and landscape, so one design covers a tall poster and a wide thumb
- A design's two lines are now simply the title and the subtitle, whatever the item is
- Text position and alignment work on every design, not just the few that had them
- New Bloom design, pooling color from the frame behind the text
- New Grid canvas, tiling several extracted frames into one picture
- Logo designs build a text logo from any name field, with letter case, a line limit, and frame-filled letters
- Frame extraction is one set of server settings instead of a copy on every design
- Frames are ranked on tone, detail, contrast, and color rather than just clearing a threshold
- Optional setting drops a subtitle that only repeats the title
- A subtitle too long to fit can shorten to its code, shrink, or trim
- Two example designs per style, each showing a genuinely different look

## Fixes
- Seasons extract from their own episodes instead of falling back to the series backdrop
- Candidate images come from different episodes instead of clustering in one
- Heavily letterboxed frames scale back up to a usable size
- Portrait text is measured against both sides, so it no longer reads small
- Brush strokes stay thick on tall posters instead of piling into a cross
- Long titles trim at a word boundary rather than mid-word
- Descenders stay inside the safe area
- Borders, rules, and shadows scale with the poster
- A static graphic keeps its proportions
- An item with no name of its own says its one line in the larger type
- Generated images carry the item's metadata language

## Developer
- The generator, the settings model, and the configuration page are rebuilt around item kinds rather than episodes
- Built against the SkiaSharp 3.119.4 and Microsoft.Extensions 10.0.11 that Jellyfin 12.0 ships
- Designs are found by reflection, so adding one needs a class and an enum value
- Every label, option, and default is read from the settings models
- The shared generator is split into pipeline, text, and overlay
- Frame analysis is a single pass, under a megabyte per frame instead of three and a half
- Every one-time upgrade of an older configuration sits in its own file, to be deleted whole once installs have moved on
- Tests hold the documentation, the templates, and US spelling to the code

## Features
- Shadows, rules, and the Frame border now scale with the poster, so they read the same on a 4K frame as on a DVD rip instead of turning into a hairline or a slab
- Long titles that do not fit two lines fill the first line with whole words and trim only the second, at a word boundary, instead of cutting both lines mid-word

## Fixes
- Frame drew no border at all for an episode without a name, and ignored the Show Title setting
- Cutout no longer lets a two line title run into the bottom of the cutout letters
- Split center-crops the series poster into its panel instead of stretching artwork that is not 2:3
- Brush honours the Show Episode setting and keeps a wrapped title inside the area the strokes leave clear
- Timeline keeps the marker dot inside the safe area on the first and last episode
- Text blocks are reserved from the font's real ascent and descent, so descenders no longer hang past the safe area

## Developer
- Built against the SkiaSharp 3.119.4 and Microsoft.Extensions 10.0.11 packages Jellyfin 12.0 ships, since the plugin binds to the server's copies at runtime
- Text drawing moved from the removed SKPaint text members to SKFont, wrapped in a shared TextStyle so every style measures and draws with the same objects
- Standard and Split share one text stack; Numeral, Cutout, Brush, and Frame no longer hand-build their own paints
- Cutout renders through a canvas layer instead of a full-size scratch bitmap per poster; Split and Brush dispose their gradient shaders
- Letterbox detection scans the pixel buffer directly instead of a native call per pixel
- Bitmap scaling uses explicit cubic resampling now that FilterQuality is gone

## Developer
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- The dashboard menu entry now shows a icon instead of the generic folder
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10, and label sync has the token scope it needs

## Features
- Generated posters now appear in the episodes Edit Images dialog, so you can pick the frame you want instead of refreshing until you get a good one
- Choose how many alternate posters to offer in Edit Images, from 1 to 10 (default 3)
- Brush style can outline its stroke, sharing the Cutout styles outline toggle
- Element Spacing setting controls the gap between stacked poster elements, so every style spaces them the same way
- The font dropdown now lists the fonts actually installed on your server, and a font that is not installed is called out in the log instead of silently rendering in a substitute face
- Overlay colors collapse to an opacity control when Palette-Derived Colors is on, since the color itself comes from the image

## Breaking
- The scheduled task has been removed. Poster generation now runs entirely as a metadata provider - use a library metadata refresh, or pick a poster from Edit Images
- Processing history and its database have been removed, along with the Reset Processing History button. Jellyfins own refresh options now decide what gets regenerated

## Fixes
- Deleting an episode poster no longer left it permanently blank; there is no tracking state left to say the episode was already done
- Changing a custom font now takes effect; it used to be left out of the change detection entirely
- A tall logo no longer overlaps the episode code beneath it
- Long episode titles wrap to two lines again instead of being shortened to one
- Short titles no longer leave a gap between the episode code and the title
- Cancelling a refresh now stops frame extraction instead of letting it run to completion
- Generated posters are no longer written to the transcode directory and left behind
- Aspect ratios like 2.35:1 now parse correctly on servers with a comma decimal separator
- Saving the Posters tab no longer hangs on a spinner when the save fails, and no longer overwrites the settings on the other tab
- Settings added in a newer version no longer break saving for configurations written by an older one

## Developer
- The frosted panel shape and the brush stroke paths are disposed even when an exception unwinds
- Poster elements are positioned by a shared measure-then-place layout column instead of each style walking its own offsets, and titles are fitted to the height they are given as well as the width
- Poster configuration is never written back during plugin startup, so a failed config load can no longer overwrite good settings with defaults
- Poster rendering returns encoded bytes rather than temp files
- Removed the scheduled task, tracking database, configuration hashing, and around 900 lines of superseded code
- Shaders, mask filters, and image filters are disposed rather than left to finalization; HDR brightening no longer round-trips the whole bitmap through managed memory
- Example templates carry every current setting, and the bundled examples were regenerated
- Test suite grown from 21 to 39 cases, covering layout, title fitting, aspect ratio parsing, font resolution, and the generated image cache
- Bump Base to 2026.7.31

## Developer
- Bump Base to 2026.7.12

## Fixes
- Remove backdrops before using the current extracted frame as the new backdrop to prevent image bloat

## Fixes
- Frame seeking starts from a random phase each run, so refreshing an episode image picks a new frame instead of the same one

## Features
- Abbreviate tries the text before a divider, then the first sentence, then initials with periods

## Fixes
- Episode numbers and codes are pinned so title length cannot move them in any style
- Fade titles wrap to two vertical rows before long title handling engages

## Features
- New Long Titles dropdown with Ellipsis, Abbreviate, and Drop Name modes for titles that do not fit

## Fixes
- Cutout no longer overflows the poster edges on long episode titles. Every style now bounds long titles
- Safe area now applies the same pixel margin on all four sides based on poster height

## Polish
- Documentation and interface text cleanup

## Features
- New poster style - Striped - tilted pinstriped sash carrying the episode title

name: Custom Pages [✓✓✓]
overview: Serve custom pages directly from your Jellyfin server with user permission restrictions for page access.
description:
Custom Pages lets administrators publish pages served by Jellyfin at /pages/{slug}. Each page can be public or restricted to users or administrators, with access enforced by Jellyfin's own authorization policies.

versions.changelog:
## Developer
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.16.

## Developer
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10
Fix 3.2 build issues.

## Developer
- Server routes moved under the Allow system access toggle, so a page needs one permission instead of two
- Shortened the configuration page help text

## Features
- Allow local resource calls, so a page can define named server side routes and call them with serverFetch while the server forwards each to its configured target
- Optional per page Allow system access toggle that runs a page without the sandbox, so its scripts can call the Jellyfin API and reach other resources on this origin
- Pages on a signed in tier can now be restricted to named users, defaulting to all users at that tier

## Developer
- Defining a route also runs its page unsandboxed, since the helper cannot reach the route from an opaque origin
- A route credential stored before encryption existed is upgraded on the next save rather than left in the clear
- Route credentials are encrypted at rest and never sent to a browser, and the configuration page posts back a sentinel so an untouched field keeps the stored value
- Forwarded requests carry the caller's headers minus a deny list, so the viewer's Jellyfin session is never handed to a route target
- Route targets must be absolute http or https URLs fixed in configuration, so a page cannot turn a route into an open proxy
- A restricted page is refused before its body is rendered, so content never reaches a viewer the list does not name
- An allow list is refused on an anonymous page at save time, and fails closed at serve time if the stored list is unusable
- Pages stay sandboxed by default, and an unsandboxed page still reaches the browser HTML encoded inside the wrapper's srcdoc
- Bump base to 2026.07.31

## Developer
- Serve every page under one Content-Security-Policy so a page behaves the same at any visibility tier
- Allow pages to load external resources and submit forms, which the anonymous tier previously blocked
- Allow pages to be embedded by the Jellyfin origin (frame-ancestors 'self')
- Serve page HTML as UTF-8 so single-file documents without a charset meta tag render correctly
- Sign in correctly when the web client is signed in to more than one server
- Reject unknown visibility tiers and malformed asset content types when configuration is saved
- Key the decoded asset cache to the asset itself, closing a stale-bytes window around a save

overview: Keep your DNS records pointed at your server's current public IP.

Dynamic DNS keeps one or more DNS records pointed at your Jellyfin server's current public IP. It runs in-process as a scheduled task and updates Cloudflare, DuckDNS, or any dyndns2-compatible provider over outbound HTTP/S.

versions.changelog:
## Developer
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.16.

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.07.31
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- The dashboard menu entry now shows a dns icon instead of the generic folder
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10, and label sync has the token scope it needs

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.07.31

## Fixed
- The plain-http warning no longer logs the request URL's authority, which carried the update secret into the server log for providers whose credential lives in the URL's userinfo (ClouDNS DynURL, Directnic gateway URL). The warning now names the record's hostname instead
- A Data Protection key store that fails for an unexpected reason surfaces instead of being silently downgraded to plaintext credential storage; the expected failures (bad path, no permission, no service) still fall back as before

## Developer
- Address the outstanding CodeQL findings across the plugin and test projects (LINQ filtering and projection, ternary assignment, dictionary lookup, response disposal in the HTTP test stub)

## Fixed
- Resolve the TTL "1 = automatic" sentinel to a per-provider default instead of sending a literal one-second TTL (Gandi, GoDaddy, Spaceship, Hetzner, DNSExit)
- Yandex matches records by type as well as name, so an IPv4 update can no longer overwrite an AAAA or TXT record, and A/AAAA now update independently
- Spaceship writes the new record before removing stale ones, so a failed update leaves the old address serving instead of deleting the record
- Hetzner treats an accepted, still-applying action as success instead of timing out and counting a false failure toward backoff
- DNS Made Easy treats "no update required" as success instead of walking a healthy record into backoff
- DDNS.fm validates the response body instead of treating any HTTP 200 as success
- NS1 record creation sends the required zone, domain, and type fields, so first-time setup works
- Apex hostnames infer the correct domain when no zone is set (Porkbun, Dynadot, Spaceship, Dinahosting), and Dinahosting gained an optional Zone field
- OVH DynHost, DynDNS v1, DSLReports, and NearlyFreeSpeech.NET declare IPv4-only, so an IPv6 address is no longer recorded as pushed and endlessly re-pushed
- A record with one working address family is no longer paused by backoff when only the other family fails

## Developer
- Harden the publish workflow (release body via env, tag-derived version, fail-fast asset downloads, required tag on manual dispatch)
- Slash-command dispatch uses the JF_BOT_TOKEN secret instead of a placeholder
- CI packages with build.sh and verifies the zip contents, and build.sh parses build.yaml colon- and space-safely
- Response-parsing tests for every provider plus orchestrator and API tests

## Developer
- Bump Base to 2026.7.12
- Use ActivityLogger from Base 2026.7.12
- Use BackoffPolicy from Base 2026.7.12

## Feature
- Output logging to Activity Logs for better visibility

## Security
- Encrypt credentials saved through the generic plugin configuration endpoint instead of waiting for the next run
- Warn in the log when a record updates over plain http
- Show a dashboard warning when credential encryption is unavailable and secrets are stored in plaintext

## Developer
- Share one SecretProtector between the dashboard and generic save paths
- Snapshot the configuration per update run instead of mutating live records

## Fixes
- Prune record status against fresh record ids so a record added mid-run is not dropped

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.6.23
- Fix encryption of tokens to ensure they will not break between versions
- Migrate everything so it lives in the provider for ease of maintenance
- Reorganize files

## Documentation
- Creates Provider documentation per ddclient

## Fixes
- Check the DNS for current IP instead of always resending
- If the current DNS is internal, use the previous IP sent (previous behavior)

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.6.19
- Fix encryption of tokens to ensure they will not break between versions

## Fixes
- Remove URL from logging

This plugin acts as a DDNS resolver using Jellyfin as its host. A lot of this work will look very similar to [ddclient](https://github.com/ddclient/ddclient) which was a huge help and inspiration for this plugin. This takes the work they've taken and wraps it into a Jellyfin plugin for server owners don't want to manage more than one application.

versions.changelog:
## Developer

- Changing which segments are avoided discards the idle frame pools, so the next refresh extracts under the new choice

- New Cleanup Backdrops scheduled task under Library that reduces every item on the server to a single backdrop, keeping the first and deleting the rest along with their files
- The task has no default schedule, so it only runs when started by hand or on a trigger you add

- Primary and thumb images can name a second and third design, adding their versions of the same frames to the Edit Images picker
- New Edit Images Cache setting for how long rendered choices stay available, default 30 minutes

- The Edit Images cache is bounded by size at 256 MB and releases expired images on its own, instead of holding them until the next render
- Every design in one Edit Images render draws from the same frames, even while other items are extracting
- Posters pass over a logo Jellyfin only knows by web address and use the next logo that can be read

## Features

- The repository moved with the name; re-add it as jellyfin-plugin-artworkgenerator to keep getting updates
- Draws posters, thumbs, backdrops, and text logos, where before there were only episode posters
- Covers series, seasons, films, music videos, home videos, and anything else with a video
- Configuration is rebuilt in three parts, designs, logos, and profiles
- Profiles decide which items get which images and which design draws each one
- Every design renders portrait and landscape, so one design covers a tall poster and a wide thumb
- A design's two lines are now simply the title and the subtitle, whatever the item is
- Text position and alignment work on every design, not just the few that had them
- New Bloom design, pooling color from the frame behind the text
- New Grid canvas, tiling several extracted frames into one picture
- Logo designs build a text logo from any name field, with letter case, a line limit, and frame-filled letters
- Frame extraction is one set of server settings instead of a copy on every design
- Frames are ranked on tone, detail, contrast, and color rather than just clearing a threshold
- Optional setting drops a subtitle that only repeats the title
- A subtitle too long to fit can shorten to its code, shrink, or trim
- Two example designs per style, each showing a genuinely different look

## Fixes
- Seasons extract from their own episodes instead of falling back to the series backdrop
- Candidate images come from different episodes instead of clustering in one
- Heavily letterboxed frames scale back up to a usable size
- Portrait text is measured against both sides, so it no longer reads small

- Descenders stay inside the safe area
- Borders, rules, and shadows scale with the poster

- Built against the SkiaSharp 3.119.4 and Microsoft.Extensions 10.0.11 that Jellyfin 12.0 ships

name: Live Channels [✓✓✓]
overview: Build looping virtual TV channels that appear natively in Jellyfin's Live TV.
description:
Live Channels lets administrators build looping virtual TV channels from genres and official ratings or from a hand-picked list of items. Each channel, its guide, and its stream are served in-process through Jellyfin's own Live TV, so the channels appear automatically with no tuner to add, no URLs to paste, and no exposed endpoints.  
  
Universal Repo 
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JPKribs/jellyfin-plugin-livechannels/master/manifest.json  
Github: https://github.com/JPKribs/jellyfin-plugin-livechannels

## Developer
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.16.

## User
- The Refresh Guide progress is now more accurate

## User
- Channels now direct play on clients that support the stream instead of always being remuxed or transcoded by the server

## Developer
- The opened source now sets SupportsDirectPlay. PlaybackInfo always disables direct stream (MediaInfoHelper), so a source that only allowed direct stream could never be picked and every tune-in fell back to DirectPlayError and a remux

## User
- A channel with no viewers now stops when its countdown reaches zero. It used to run on for two to three minutes after the last viewer left
- Tune-in cards are generated for every channel shortly after the server starts and at every guide refresh, including the refresh a save triggers, so a fresh install, an update, a new logo, or changed output settings never leave a channel opening without its card

## Developer
- The linger teardown was vetoed every time because the Jellyfin reader is served right up to the close, so the two-minute recent-delivery rule always saw a viewer at the 30s mark, and the one-shot task then gave up until the reaper backstop 90s plus a minute later. A lingering session now only counts delivery after the close (DeliveryCountsAsWatched, unit tested), and LingerTeardownAsync retries every 5s until the reaper threshold
- LiveChannelsTvService sweeps the tune-in cards 20s after construction and from every GetChannelsAsync (EnsureLogoAsync then IntroService.EnsureAsync per enabled channel, serialised, logged with its trigger); a tune-in without a card now logs it
- The Sessions tab countdown wording no longer uses an em dash or a semicolon

## User
- Tune-in is now immediate. A channel opens on a short animated card (its logo and a Starting Channel caption over flowing lines) the moment you tune in, while the content is seeked and encoded behind it, and the picture no longer waits ten seconds or more for a buffer to fill first
- The Start-up buffer setting is gone. It turned out to be a literal pause Jellyfin applied before every tune-in rather than a buffer, and the cushion it was meant to provide is now built up while you are already watching

## Developer
- Removed StartupBufferSeconds and BufferMs (Jellyfin sleeps for BufferMs in TranscodeManager.AcquireResources before launching the delivery ffmpeg, on every tune-in including adoption)
- The tune-in handover now waits for the playlist and one segment instead of the full cushion, and the endpoint reader's hold-back ramps in one segment per ten seconds of session age instead of applying from the first byte
- Segments and the encoder GOP are now three seconds, matching Jellyfin's delivery remux so every stage cuts on the same keyframes

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.07.31
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- The dashboard menu entry now shows a live_tv icon instead of the generic folder
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10, and label sync has the token scope it needs

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.07.31

## Developer
- A channel whose filters legitimately match nothing now reuses its cached empty schedule instead of re running the full library resolve on every tune in
- Guide refreshes no longer pin every enabled channel's decoded schedule in memory forever, only channels actually being watched keep a hot copy
- Long running time of day channels now resume their schedule chain where the last window ended instead of re simulating it from the anchor at every refill, so the walk no longer grows with session length
- Code scanning cleanup across the encoder resolver, stress test, recording copy, and tune in deadline, with no behaviour changes

## Developer
- A custom stream file location is validated at save and marked on disk, and cleanup only ever deletes the plugin's own session folders, so pointing it at a folder with existing content can no longer delete that content
- Settings saved through the API are validated like the dashboard enforces them, so an out of range resolution, bitrate, session limit, or channel number is rejected with a reason instead of silently breaking streams later
- The Popular Channel's settings are validated like every other channel's
- The channel editor now edits a copy, so only Save channel persists its changes, switching channels asks before discarding unsaved edits, and a failed save shows the server's reason
- An item with a broken production year can no longer take down a chronological channel's guide build
- Generated logos and the icon font moved from the shared system temp folder into Jellyfin's cache
- Tuning in to a channel cancels a running stress test, so a real viewer always wins the encoder
- The plugin now correctly declares Jellyfin 10.11.10 as its minimum server version

## Developer
- Guide programs now carry a poster, a landscape thumb, a backdrop, and a logo instead of one image, with episodes taking their poster from the series, so every client renders the shape its layout wants
- New Start up buffer setting, defaulting to 12 seconds, sets how much of a channel is encoded before playback starts and how far ahead of you it stays. Raise it if the first seconds of a tune in stutter
- Burned in subtitles now come from the file Jellyfin extracts, so bold, italic, and colour markup survives, external subtitle files burn correctly, and attached fonts are used
- {'New subtitle appearance settings': 'font, size, text and outline colour, outline or solid box background, and bold. Untouched, subtitles render exactly as authored'}
- Streams Jellyfin reports as playing, paused included, are never closed by the stream cap, the time limit, or the idle timer. Only Kill on the Sessions tab stops a stream someone is watching
- An encoder that dies mid watch is replaced in place, continuing where it stopped, instead of ending the stream

## Developer
- Timers now produce real recordings. When a timer's window ends the aired program is resolved back to the library item it replayed and that file is placed in the Live TV recordings folder, hardlinked on the same volume or copied otherwise, with no capture or transcoding
- Recordings use the built in DVR's folder and naming scheme, honoring the server's configured recording paths and subfolder option, so they land as Series/Season folders and Movie (Year) folders the recordings library groups correctly
- The recordings folder is registered as a library when nothing serves it and a targeted refresh runs after each recording, so new recordings appear on the Recordings shelf immediately
- Record Series now works. One rule per series per channel (duplicate rules consolidate automatically and their timers follow the surviving rule), expanding into linked upcoming timers a day ahead, one per distinct episode, honoring day and time constraints. Cancelling a rule removes it and its timers
- Cancelling a timer sticks and aborts it in place, so no recording is delivered. Cancelled timers become tombstones series expansion cannot recreate, and pressing record again re arms the program
- Completed timers carry their recording path and age out of the timer list while the recording lives on as a normal library item. Failed recordings retry up to three times before the timer is marked errored
- Recording a program that already aired works, since the content it replayed already exists
